subject: Geography
central_question: How do pressure differences and wind-driving forces produce global circulation, local winds, air-mass interactions and major weather systems?
in_scope_units: Atmospheric pressure and vertical and horizontal variation
Forces affecting wind and geostrophic flow
El Nino, Southern Oscillation and ENSO
banned_topics: Detailed condensation and rainfall classification from Chapter 10
Detailed monsoon mechanism reserved for India: Physical Environment

known_pitfalls.claim: Wind direction is controlled only by the pressure gradient force.
known_pitfalls.correction: Near the surface pressure-gradient, frictional and Coriolis forces act together, with gravity acting downward.

known_pitfalls.claim: Coriolis force is strongest at the equator.
known_pitfalls.correction: It is absent at the equator and increases with latitude.

known_pitfalls.claim: Tropical and extra-tropical cyclones form in the same way.
known_pitfalls.correction: Extra-tropical cyclones are frontal mid/high-latitude systems; tropical cyclones form over warm tropical oceans.

known_pitfalls.claim: El Nino is only an ocean-temperature change.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter links El Nino with Pacific pressure changes called the Southern Oscillation; together they are ENSO.
